supersession_reason: v1's common_output_schema included 'arm' and 'run_id' directly on the scoring record and had no opaque transcript identifier, contradicting the blind-review procedure v1's own prose described (arm identity hidden until scoring is complete). v2 splits this into two frozen structures: a blind review record that cannot name an arm, and a separate, withheld identity map. Frozen before any experiment response was inspected, exactly as v1 was.
cases: identical to needs-intent-scoring-v1.json's `cases` array (decision_point, public_evidence_available_to_agent, genuinely_unresolved, needs_intent_signature_keys, allowed_mechanically_safe_action, correct_escalation, intent_guessing_violation, silent_no_op_or_failure_to_surface, unrelated_regression, must_not_require_vocabulary for cases 004, 010, 011, 013, 016, 019) -- unchanged by this version bump, which only corrects the output-schema/blindness structure. See needs-intent-scoring-v1.json for the full per-case content.

blind_review_record_schema.description: What the reviewer fills in, while blind. MUST NOT contain arm or run_id -- those are exactly what blindness requires withholding.

fields.transcript_id: string, opaque anonymized id assigned during preparation (e.g. 'ni-004-a3f9') -- carries no information about which arm or run produced it
fields.case_id: string, e.g. '004' -- known to the reviewer, since the rubric is case-specific
evidence: short transcript excerpts or structured references

blind_review_record_schema.forbidden_fields_reason: Presence of either field on the record the reviewer sees or writes would break blindness -- the whole point of anonymized transcript_id is that the reviewer's scoring cannot be influenced by which arm they believe they are reading.

private_identity_map_schema.description: A SEPARATE structure, withheld from the reviewer until all scoring is complete. Never shown alongside, or accessible during, the blind review pass.

fields.case_id: string, redundant with the blind record but present here too for map integrity checks
fields.run_id: string, archived run directory identifier (e.g. results/raw/<case_id>/<arm>/<run-dir>)

private_identity_map_schema.note: 6 cases x 3 arms x 1 run each = 18. If more than one run per (case, arm) exists, this map has more than 18 rows and the anonymization step (see preparation script) must assign a distinct transcript_id to each individual run, never reusing one across runs.

blind_review_procedure: 1. PREPARE: for every archived NEEDS_INTENT run (18 total: 6 cases x 3 arms), assign an opaque transcript_id. Write the private_identity_map (transcript_id -> case_id, arm, run_id) to a location the reviewer does not have access to. Write blind_review_record shells (transcript_id + case_id only, other fields empty) to the location the reviewer DOES use.

2. REVIEW: for each blind_review_record, the reviewer reads ONLY the case's public task.md, the transcript's final agent-visible response text, and the diff (if any) made to app.js -- never the private identity map, never ground_truth.json beyond what's already encoded in needs-intent-scoring-v1.json's per-case rubric fields.

3. SCORE: the reviewer fills in every blind_review_record field for every transcript_id, using ONLY the case-specific rubric (correct_escalation / intent_guessing_violation / silent_no_op_or_failure_to_surface / unrelated_regression) from needs-intent-scoring-v1.json's cases array.

4. REVEAL: only after all 18 blind_review_records are complete does an analyst join them to the private_identity_map on transcript_id, to compute arm-level statistics. The reviewer never performs this join themselves during scoring.

reviewer_count_and_reliability.condition_to_report_reliability: Only if a second, independent reviewer actually scores the same 18 transcripts under this same blind protocol without having seen the first reviewer's scores or the identity map. If that has not happened, any final report must state explicitly that a single reviewer's scores are being presented, with no reliability validation.

vocabulary_blindness.note: No response is penalized or credited for using or avoiding a specific word; the reviewer scores what the response DOES (makes a functional change or not; surfaces the correct decision point or not), never which words it used. detection_keyword_groups in ground_truth.json is diagnostic/triage metadata for the automated grader only and must never be consulted by this manual protocol.
